title: Off-diagonal evaluation kernel for the algebra of sequences over a field
statement: Let $K$ be a field [def-weil-field], and let $B=\prod_{n\geq1}K$ be the commutative $K$-algebra of all sequences, with coordinatewise operations and diagonal scalar map. Write $C=B\otimes_K B$ for the algebraic module tensor product [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], endowed with the commutative algebra multiplication $(u\otimes v)(u\prime\otimes v\prime)=uu\prime\otimes vv\prime$ and unit $1\otimes1$. Let $e_n\in B$ be $1$ at coordinate $n$ and $0$ at every other coordinate. Define the $K$-algebra homomorphism $\theta:C\to\prod_{n\ne m}K$ by $\theta(u\otimes v)_{n,m}=u_n v_m$. Then $\ker\theta=(e_n\otimes e_n\mid n\geq1)$, the ideal of $C$ generated by the displayed diagonal tensors.

source.place: Tag 088I (lemma-infinite-number), proof: the kernel generated by diagonal coordinate idempotents, specialized to a constant family of fields.

proof.text: Let $t\in\ker\theta$. By the generating clause of [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], write $t=\sum_{i=1}^r u_i\otimes v_i$, absorbing scalar coefficients into $u_i$. The subspace $U=\operatorname{span}_K\{u_1,\ldots,u_r\}\subseteq B$ is finite-dimensional by [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace]. Reindex sequences by $j\mapsto j+1$ and apply [lem-weil-finite-coordinate-detection] to $U$. Obtain a finite $S\subseteq\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$ such that a member of $U$ vanishing on $S$ is zero. For each $m$, put $c_m=\sum_i v_i(m)u_i\in U$. If $m\notin S$, then $c_m(s)=\theta(t)_{s,m}=0$ for every $s\in S$, so $c_m=0$.

source.place: Tag 088I, lemma-infinite-number, proof, displayed off-diagonal map and its asserted kernel (lines 3480–3486); detailed constant-field argument supplied here.

proof.text: For $m\in S$ and $n\ne m$, $c_m(n)=\theta(t)_{n,m}=0$. Thus $c_m=a_m e_m$, where $a_m=c_m(m)$. Set $d=\sum_{m\in S}a_m(e_m\otimes e_m)$ and $w=t-d$. The column at $m$ of $d$ is $a_m e_m$ if $m\in S$, and zero otherwise. Hence every column of $w$ is zero, including its diagonal entry. These assertions follow by evaluating the finite sums; they also hold when $S$ is empty.

source.place: Tag 088I, lemma-infinite-number, proof, displayed off-diagonal map and its asserted kernel (lines 3480–3486); detailed constant-field argument supplied here.

proof.text: We justify that zero columns imply $w=0$, using [lem-sfb-vector-space-tensor-family-zero-detection]. Write $w=\sum_j x_j\otimes y_j$ using [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. The bilinear flip defines $\tau:B\otimes_K B\to B\otimes_K B$, $x\otimes y\mapsto y\otimes x$, with $\tau^2=1$ by the generating clause. For $f_m:B\to K$, $f_m(y)=y(m)$, the image $(f_m\otimes\mathrm{id}_B)(\tau w)$ in $K\otimes_K B$ equals $\sum_j y_j(m)\otimes x_j=1\otimes(\sum_j y_j(m)x_j)=0$: the vector in parentheses is precisely the zero column at $m$. The middle equality is bilinear balancing, not an identification of infinite products with tensor products. The family $(f_m)_m$ detects zero because a function with every value zero is zero. Apply the cited detection lemma with $M=N=B$ and $P_m=K$ to obtain $\tau w=0$; apply $\tau$ again to get $w=0$.

source.place: Tag 088I, lemma-infinite-number, proof, displayed off-diagonal map and its asserted kernel (lines 3480–3486); detailed constant-field argument supplied here.

proof.text: Therefore $t=d$ is a finite $K$-linear combination of the generators $e_m\otimes e_m$, so it belongs to their generated ideal. Conversely, each generator has zero evaluation at every pair $n\ne m$. Sums of multiples of these generators still have zero evaluation, since $\theta$ is an algebra homomorphism. This proves both ideal inclusions.
